screen.dimblend_experience.tuning.shake_: Default: 2.0 seconds. Range: 0.1-60.0, step: 0.1. 0 disables random draws.
screen.dimblend_experience.tuning.brake_: Default: 1. Signals at or below the cap pass through unchanged; stronger signals are clamped to the cap (brake strength and kinetic network stress follow the adjusted signal). 15 restores vanilla scaling.
Default: 2.0 m/s. Range: 0.0-64.0 m/s, step: 0.1. The brake sound plays only while bogey speed is strictly above this threshold; the release sound is not gated.
screen.dimblend_experience.tuning.deadma: Default: 32. Range: 8-128 blocks, step: 1. Rotating dimension only: distance is measured against the whole consist (carriages joined by automatic couplers form one train) — a player counts as attending when the consist's nearest bogie to them is within this radius, regardless of that bogie's own speed; when a moving consist (>4 m/s anywhere in it) has nobody attending, the whole consist is force-braked; any raw redstone level change on any bogie immediately releases that entire consist, including rising, falling and powered-to-powered changes. Other consists keep their own brake state.
screen.dimblend_experience.tuning.bogie_: Default: 5000 (Simurail's own default). Range: 0-10000000, step: 1. Caps the torque each bogie's roll spring may use to keep the car body upright (Simurail's bogeyAngularSpringMaxTorque). Raise it if tall or heavy cars lean over on their bogies; the spring's stiffness is unchanged, so only cars that hit the cap respond. 0 removes the roll spring; cars then rest on the bogie's 15° roll stop. With 1 Sable sub-step per tick, values far above the default can make cars shudder; keep 2 sub-steps. Applies on the next physics step and is saved in Simurail's server config.
screen.dimblend_experience.tuning.soilin: Default: 0.5. Range: 0.00-1.00, step: 0.01. Chance = min(1, speed / 12 x multiplier). 0 disables dirtiness draws.
screen.dimblend_experience.tuning.couple: Default: off. Allows redstone signals to unlock automatic couplers.
Default: off. Allows Survival players to interact with automatic couplers.
screen.dimblend_experience.tuning.sable_: Vehicle headlights
Default: on. Custom lighting for lit Design n Decor frontlights, on Sable vehicles and placed in the world alike. Requires Veil; disabled with Iris.
Headlight range
Default: 24 blocks. Range: 4-64, step 0.5. Light fades smoothly to zero at this distance.
Headlight cone angle
Default: 50 degrees. Full cone angle: 10-120, step 1.
Headlight intensity
Default: 1.00. Range: 0-3, step 0.05. Zero disables the light pass; the lamp texture stays lit.
Headlight beam haze
Default: on. Adds warm volumetric haze inside headlight cones and a soft glow at the lens.
Headlight haze density
Default: 0.35. Range: 0-2, step 0.01. Zero skips haze rendering.
Headlight haze samples
Default: 8. Range: 4-24, step 1. More samples reduce noise at a higher GPU cost.
Headlight shadows
Default: on. Solid blocks of the world and of vehicles block headlight light and haze (glass, leaves and fluids let it through). Off saves a little CPU and GPU time.
Headlight lava highlight

Default: on. Wraps lava a lit headlight beam reaches in a gently pulsing orange wireframe box (2x2x2 per block, touching boxes merged); parts behind walls, terrain and vehicles show dimmed. Follows the headlight and shadow options; the world is re-scanned ten times a second only while a beam moves.
screen.dimblend_experience.tuning.observ: Default: 32 blocks. Range: 16-64, step 1. An observer blaze emits redstone strength 15 while a lit searchlight beam marks lava whose top-face centre is within this distance of it. Requires the headlight and lava highlight options.
item.dimblend_experience.searchlight.fro: Right-click with an amethyst shard to enable searchlight mode
Searchlight mode detects and marks lava threats
item.dimblend_experience.searchlight.obs: Right-click with a spyglass to make it guard the train
Emits a redstone signal when it detects a marked lava threat
screen.dimblend_experience.tuning.sky_ti: Default: off. Record this client's sky/time changes in logs/latest.log. Changes apply immediately and are saved locally; other players are unaffected.
screen.dimblend_experience.tuning.copper: Default: off. Off uses a finite 2000 mB tank. Enabling also requires Create Fluid to allow infiniteWater.
screen.dimblend_experience.tuning.limite: Default: on. Checks new source water in the rotating dimension. The ice placement rule has its own setting.
screen.dimblend_experience.tuning.sable_: Structure-void fitting on vehicles
Default: on. Fits the world-space volume of Sable vehicles with structure voids so water cannot flow into a moving vehicle. Fitted cells are never written to the save.
Lava melting vehicle blocks

Default: on. Lava and flowing lava melt blocks on Sable structures at the sable_lava_melt_speed rate (default 4x bare-hand breaking speed) and drop them as items; hardness only sets the pace, obsidian-grade takes about a minute at the default rate; components on the machine-unbreakable list (bogies, automatic couplers) are immune. While on, structure-void fitting no longer evicts lava. Requires Sable.
Lava melt speed multiplier

Default: 4.0. Speed multiplier (relative to bare-hand breaking) for lava melting blocks on Sable structures, 0.5-64.0 in steps of 0.1; obsidian-grade takes about a minute at 4.0. Changes apply on the fly and keep accumulated melt progress. Requires Sable.
Void-fit vehicles per scan

Default: 2. How many vehicles a structure-void fitting scan may refit per cycle; the rest go first in the next round. Raise it when many vehicles share one dimension to relieve scan starvation. Requires Sable.
Lava melt vehicles per scan
Default: 2. How many vehicles the lava melt scan processes per 5-tick round (round-robin cursor). Raise it when many vehicles share one dimension to relieve scan starvation. Requires Sable.
screen.dimblend_experience.tuning.portab: Default: on. Allows only one Portable Engine per connected kinetic network, including stopped networks.
screen.dimblend_experience.tuning.steam_: Default: on. Sustained overload breaks the shaft. Disabling clears active warnings and exhaust effects.
screen.dimblend_experience.tuning.diesel: Default: on. Applies to Small, Modular and Large engines. Disabling cancels pending destruction and clears overload latches.
screen.dimblend_experience.tuning.motor_: Default: on. Overload locks the output and doubles energy use. Disabling clears the overload latch.
screen.dimblend_experience.tuning.radio_: Default: 0.50 (the former on level). Range: 0.00-2.00, step: 0.01. Scales the static, crackle and voices: 0 plays every radio clean, 2.00 is four times the former level. Overworld and underground play clean; the Nether and modded areas add faint static; the End lets faint enderman and shulker voices through now and then; Voidscape plays static only.

Default: 2.0 (twice the original rate). Range: 0.0-4.0, step: 0.1. 1.0 restores the original first wait of 10-30 seconds and subsequent spacing of 25-70 seconds; 0 disables new voices. Enderman and shulker ambient clips are selected with weights 7 and 1.

Default: 0.75 (1.5 times the former hard-coded gain). Range: 0.00-2.00, step: 0.01. 0.5 restores the former loudness; 0 schedules no enderman or shulker voices at all, so the music is not ducked either.
Default: 1.00. Range: 0.00-2.00, step: 0.01. Scales the simulated echo (reflections and reverb). 0 leaves only the direct sound, which keeps its occlusion and 3D direction.
screen.dimblend_experience.tuning.exp_cl: Default: 1.00 (clears all). Range: 0.00-1.00, step: 0.01. Rotating dimension only: respawn experience = pre-death x (1 - ratio), ignoring the keepInventory game rule; experience orbs never drop.
screen.dimblend_experience.tuning.rotati: Default: 50. Range: 0-100, step: 1. Density of covered monster spawns in the rotating dimension as a percentage of vanilla (100 = vanilla density, 0 = no covered monster spawns). Natural spawning both scales the global cap and keeps each spawn with this probability; spawner, trial spawner, structure, chunk generation, patrol and reinforcement spawns cancel with probability 1 - p. Bosses and player-caused spawns (spawn egg, command, breeding, conversion, ...) are never suppressed; other dimensions and categories are unaffected.
screen.dimblend_experience.tuning.item_d: Item drain growth boost water cost (mB)
Default: 20. Range: 0-1500, step: 1. Water drained per successful growth boost (1000 mB = 1 bucket); 0 = free boosts.
screen.dimblend_experience.tuning.sable_: Sable physics sub-steps per tick
Default: 2. Range: 1-10, step: 1. Recommended: 1. Higher values are significantly more performance-intensive but more accurate.
Sable solver iterations
Default: 18. Range: 1-64, step: 1. Recommended: 6. Constraint-solver force iterations; fewer iterations save solver CPU but soften joints and contacts.
Sable PGS iterations
Default: 2. Range: 1-8, step: 1. Recommended: 2. PGS iterations run by the constraint solver.
Sable stabilization iterations
Default: 2. Range: 1-8, step: 1. Recommended: 2. Stabilization iterations run by the constraint solver.
Sable physics tick interval

Default: 1. Range: 1-10, step: 1. Recommended: 1. Values above 1 simulate every N ticks with a proportionally larger time step; 2 is an experimental half-rate mode that halves physics CPU at the cost of choppier motion.
Sable sleep skip
Default: on. Recommended: on. Lets the physics engine skip simulating sleeping bodies.
Sable contact force events
Default: on. Recommended: off. Reports contact force events used for collision sounds and particles; turning this off saves the callback cost but vehicles lose collision sound and particle feedback.
Sable biome projection fast path
Default: on. Recommended: on. Skips sub-level biome projection lookups in dimensions that have no sub-levels.
Sable empty-container fast path
Default: on. Recommended: on. Skips per-tick sub-level container work in dimensions that have no sub-levels and no pending sub-level storage or ticket work.
screen.dimblend_experience.perf.title: Performance checklist
screen.dimblend_experience.perf.summary_: %s of %s steps still need attention. Click a row to open it.
Applying the fix on the server…
The fix failed; see the game log.
This fix is not available here.
The server did not answer; only this computer's steps are shown.
screen.dimblend_experience.perf.spark_ba: spark's background profiler samples all the time. On Windows it can only use its Java sampler, which freezes every game thread for each sample: in our captures that meant about 100 freezes per second, with single freezes of 100-300 ms. Turning it off keeps spark installed; you can still start a profile by hand.
Set by backgroundProfiler in config/spark/config.json on the server.
On. Use the button below to turn it off in the config. It stops after the next restart; to stop it right away, also run /spark profiler cancel.
Turned off in the config. Restart the game or server for it to take effect, or run /spark profiler cancel to stop it now.
spark is not installed on the server. Nothing to do.
screen.dimblend_experience.perf.gc_colle: While the garbage collector pauses, the whole game stops. With G1 we measured pauses of up to 136 ms; Java 21's generational ZGC keeps pauses around a millisecond, provided the heap has enough headroom (next step).
Non-generational ZGC. Add -XX:+ZGenerational to the JVM arguments in your launcher.
G1. Add -XX:+UseZGC -XX:+ZGenerational to the JVM arguments in your launcher, then check heap headroom (next step).
Not ZGC. Add -XX:+UseZGC -XX:+ZGenerational to the JVM arguments in your launcher.
screen.dimblend_experience.perf.heap_hea: The memory still in use right after a collection is what the game really needs. With too little room above it, collections run back to back, and ZGC can stall threads that need memory until a collection finishes.
%1$s GiB still in use after the last collection, of %2$s GiB maximum (%3$s%%).
Getting tight. Raise -Xmx to at least %4$sG in your launcher, if the machine has that much free memory (next step).
Too little headroom. Raise -Xmx to at least %4$sG in your launcher, if the machine has that much free memory (next step).
screen.dimblend_experience.perf.system_m: When the computer runs out of physical memory, Windows moves game memory to the page file. Touching it again stalls the game for tens to hundreds of milliseconds and makes every pause above longer.
%1$s GiB of %2$s GiB physical memory free; %3$s GiB of page file in use.
Enough free memory. Nothing to do.
Free memory is low. Close other heavy programs before playing, and do not raise -Xmx beyond what is free.
Almost no free memory. Close other heavy programs; until then the game will keep stuttering.
screen.dimblend_experience.perf.async_sa: The server autosaves every 5 minutes. Without dimblend_asyncsave, compressing and writing level.dat and player data happens on the server thread and stalls that tick by up to half a second.
Checks that dimblend_asyncsave is installed on the server and that its mixins are loaded.
Installed and active. Nothing to do.
Installed, but its mixins are not loaded, so saves still block. Update dimblend_asyncsave to a build whose neoforge.mods.toml declares its mixins.
Not installed. Add dimblend_asyncsave to the server's mods folder.
screen.dimblend_experience.perf.finite_w: FiniteWater does a full biome lookup for every water-source check. When the train reaches new terrain, freshly generated chunks run thousands of these checks at once; in our capture this was 37% of the slow-tick time.
Checks whether finite_water is installed on the server.
Installed. Remove it from the mods folder if dimblend's limited-water rule is enough for you; water sources can then form anywhere again outside the rotating dimension.
screen.dimblend_experience.perf.overworl: While nobody is in the overworld, vanilla stops ticking its mobs after 15 seconds, but the spawn-chunk ticket (game rule spawnChunkRadius) keeps a 7x7 area around world spawn loaded, plus a wide ring of partly loaded chunks around it, for the whole session. That memory and its remaining per-tick work buy nothing on this server.
spawnChunkRadius %1$s; force-loaded chunks %2$s; overworld chunks loaded right now %3$s.
Nothing keeps the overworld loaded. Nothing to do.

Use the button below to set spawnChunkRadius to 0. World spawn then loads only while someone is near it, so anything built to keep running in the spawn chunks (farms, clocks) stops while nobody is there.
%2$s chunks are force-loaded with /forceload. If you do not need them, run /execute in minecraft:overworld run forceload remove all.
screen.dimblend_experience.perf.simulati: Mob spawning, mob ticking and the work for chunks entering the simulated area all grow with this distance. Going from 12 to 8 cuts the simulated area from 625 to 289 chunks.
Use the button below to set it to %2$s.
Set simulation-distance=%2$s in server.properties and restart the server.
screen.dimblend_experience.perf.render_d: In singleplayer the built-in server loads chunks out to this distance, so a moving train keeps reading and generating terrain along that whole front. It also costs frame time on this computer.
Use the button below to set it to %2$s.
screen.dimblend_experience.perf.sable_ph: Sub-steps and solver iterations trade physics CPU for stability. In our slow-tick captures Sable physics was only about 8% of the time, so lowering them gains little while trains may jitter more.
Sub-steps %1$s, solver iterations %2$s, PGS %3$s, stabilization %4$s, physics tick interval %5$s.
Changed from Sable's defaults (2 sub-steps; 18 / 2 / 2 iterations; interval 1). If trains jitter, open the Sable page and reset them.
Sable is not installed on the server.
screen.dimblend_experience.perf.sable_in: This computer shows vehicles slightly in the past so it can blend between server updates. If an update is later than this buffer plus one tick, vehicles freeze and then jump. A longer buffer hides longer stalls but shows vehicles a little later.
Use the button below to set it to %2$s ticks, which hides stalls up to about 200 ms.
Sable is not installed on this computer.
